headline_marked: 255 votes: [[Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected]] as Bangladesh's 23rd president
headline: 255 votes: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected as Bangladesh's 23rd president
summary: The BNP leader defeated opponent Oli Ahmed by a margin of 167 votes to secure the presidency.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. He secured 255 votes to win the election.
He defeated the opposition candidate, Oli Ahmed, by a margin of 167 votes. The Election Commission has already issued a gazette notification declaring him the winner.
Following the announcement, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina greeted the President-elect with red roses, and the two were seen embracing.
The defeated candidate, Oli Ahmed, and the Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer also extended their congratulations to Mirza Fakhrul.
Shafiqur Rahman congratulated him, stating that as the guardian of the state, he hopes Fakhrul will uphold democracy in the country.
The victory has sparked celebrations in Thakurgaon, the home district of the newly elected president.
caption:
From the streets to Bangabhaban: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is now the 23rd President of Bangladesh.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. He secured 255 votes to win the election.

He defeated the opposition candidate, Oli Ahmed, by a margin of 167 votes. The Election Commission has already issued a gazette notification declaring him the winner.

Following the announcement, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina greeted the President-elect with red roses, and the two were seen embracing.

The defeated candidate, Oli Ahmed, and the Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer also extended their congratulations to Mirza Fakhrul.

Shafiqur Rahman congratulated him, stating that as the guardian of the state, he hopes Fakhrul will uphold democracy in the country.

The victory has sparked celebrations in Thakurgaon, the home district of the newly elected president.

headline_marked: China and UK congratulate [[Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on his election as president]]
headline: China and UK congratulate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on his election as president
summary: Global powers and national leaders, including Prof. Yunus, congratulate the new president, while Jamaat-e-Islami urges him to rise above party politics.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the President of Bangladesh. The announcement has triggered a wave of congratulations from both domestic and international leaders.

China has expressed its readiness to work closely with Dhaka to strengthen bilateral relations. The Chinese embassy stated it aims to build a 'China-Bangladesh community with a shared future in the new era.'
The United Kingdom has also sent its congratulations to the President-elect, signaling international support for the constitutional process.
Domestically, Chief Adviser Prof. Muhammad Yunus and Home Minister Anwarul Islam has congratulated Mirza Fakhrul on his election.
Oli Ahmed and the Ameer of Jamaat-e-Islami have also extended their greetings. Jamaat-e-Islami specifically urged the new president to rise above party politics in his new role.
Mirza Fakhrul's journey to the presidency is being described as a transition from a student activist to the Bangabhaban.
caption:
From student activist to Bangabhaban. Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is the new President of Bangladesh.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the President of Bangladesh. The announcement has triggered a wave of congratulations from both domestic and international leaders.

China has expressed its readiness to work closely with Dhaka to strengthen bilateral relations. The Chinese embassy stated it aims to build a 'China-Bangladesh community with a shared future in the new era.'

The United Kingdom has also sent its congratulations to the President-elect, signaling international support for the constitutional process.

Domestically, Chief Adviser Prof. Muhammad Yunus and Home Minister Anwarul Islam has congratulated Mirza Fakhrul on his election.

Oli Ahmed and the Ameer of Jamaat-e-Islami have also extended their greetings. Jamaat-e-Islami specifically urged the new president to rise above party politics in his new role.

Mirza Fakhrul's journey to the presidency is being described as a transition from a student activist to the Bangabhaban.
